title: Unveiling the Atomic Vibrational Anisotropy and Electron-Phonon Coupling via Momentum-Selective Electron Microscopy
content: Studying individual vibrational modes is essential for understanding optical, thermal, and superconducting phenomena in a wide range of crystalline materials and their heterostructures. At the atomic level, vibrational trajectories, known as thermal ellipsoids, exhibit significant anisotropies due to local symmetries and are traditionally analyzed using optical and diffraction methods [1]. However, the limited spatial and energy resolutions of these techniques result in measurements averaged over large crystal volumes and the entire phonon spectrum, preventing a detailed understanding of individual mode contributions to thermal and photonic responses as well as electron-phonon coupling (EPC) at interfaces. State-of-the-art monochromated electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) enables nanoscale phonon spectroscopy with energy resolutions of just a few meV [2]. Recently, we developed a momentum-selective dark-field vibrational EELS method to extract vibrational spectra with atomic displacements along specific directions. In this talk, we will demonstrate its application through two case studies: the local atomic vibrational anisotropies dictated by local symmetries in perovskite oxides and the EPC at an insulator/superconductor interface.
